title: Publish the STEM Robotics & Hardware Lab Cohort Sprint Blueprint for Maker Academies, by Fri 18 Dec
description:
Hardware engineering, robotics, and embedded systems bootcamps face unique operational hurdles: students assemble physical circuit boards, debug microcontroller firmware, and collaborate across remote benches where text chat alone fails. Instructors need a unified platform to inspect wiring, distribute schematics, and run multi-team hardware sprint demos. This blueprint establishes Zedu as the operating system for physical-computing cohort academies.

Work under this goal:
- Design the hardware lab pod workspace architecture: multi-team prototype channels (#hardware-squad-1, #firmware-lab), component supply channels (#bom-requests), and lab safety broadcasts.
- Write the 15-minute live hardware bench video debugging protocol utilizing native Zedu Buzz screen-sharing and multi-camera inspection workflows.
- Standardize the schematic and PCB design review protocol using Zedu's 440px discussion thread drawer for line-by-line component feedback.
- Build the bill-of-materials (BOM) and firmware hex file distribution directory structure inside Zedu File Management with versioned download access.

Done when: A comprehensive maker-academy sprint kit is delivered containing lab channel hierarchies, bench debugging run sheets, circuit review thread templates, and BOM file sharing guides verified against production zedu-fe controls.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A standard "bench report" post per debug request: photo, schematic version, firmware commit and serial log
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Remote hardware debugging fails when the instructor can't see the setup. Approach: one thread per team per sprint, and every help request uses a fixed bench report: a photo of the wiring, the schematic file version from the team's Files folder, the firmware commit or version, the serial log excerpt, and what was expected. The instructor answers in-thread so fixes are searchable later. Done: the bench report template, the Files folder naming convention for schematics and firmware, and three worked examples (wrong pin, power issue, firmware bug).
